title: Home-Site Lease Collections Standard: Nonpayment Notices, Default and Reinstatement
content:
**Collections standard — Home-Site Lease**

**A. Serving.** A nonpayment notice is served on an active lease when a billing period's rent is still unpaid more than the lot class's notice days past due after its due date, unless a repayment agreement covering that balance is current.

**B. Amount and deadline — no longer in force.** The former clause setting the amount demanded at the rent balance on the notice date and the cure deadline at the notice date plus the days listed for the community, is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis for the amount demanded and the cure deadline.

**C. Default.** A lease is placed in default only after the cure deadline has passed, counted from the nonpayment notice date. The notice date and the cure deadline are those recorded on the nonpayment notice among the lease's notices. The boundary is exclusive: a lease is never placed in default on the deadline day itself, only from the following day.

**D. Counting the cure period — no longer in force.** The former clause counting the cure period in calendar days starting the day after the notice date, with a payment received on the deadline day itself in time, is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis for running the cure period.

**E. Cure by payment — no longer in force.** The former clause by which paying the full amount demanded by the deadline cures the notice and the lease stays active, while a smaller payment is refused under the payment acceptance terms, is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis for curing a nonpayment notice.

**F. Reinstatement.** A lease in default is reinstated to active when every amount past due on the ledger, including fees posted after the notice, is paid before possession is returned.

**G. Termination.** Termination of a lease in default runs through the community's attorney and the courts. The resident desk never sets, promises or negotiates a termination, move-out or possession date, and such requests go to a human representative.

**Days listed for each community (the community's cure days)**

| Community | Days listed |
|---|---|
| Willow Bend Estates | 5 |
| Palmetto Shores | 5 |
| Saguaro Vista | 7 |
| Bluebonnet Ridge | 10 |
| Cedar Hollow | 7 |
| Conestoga Meadows | 20 |

**Paragraph A at its boundary (hypothetical; rent due on the 1st, notice days 10)** — on the 11th the rent is ten days past due and no notice is yet served; on the 12th it is more than ten days past due and the notice is served if the rent is still unpaid and no current repayment agreement covers the balance.

**Status path**

| From | To | When |
|---|---|---|
| active | in default | the cure deadline on a written nonpayment notice passes without the demanded amount being paid in full |
| in default | active | every amount past due is paid and the community reinstates the lease |
| in default | closed | the lease is terminated for nonpayment through the legal process and possession returns to the community |

superseded_clauses: The amount demanded is the rent_balance on the notice date, and the cure deadline is the notice date plus the days listed for the community in nonpayment_cure_days.
The cure period is counted in calendar days starting the day after the notice date, and a payment received on the deadline day itself is in time.
Paying the full amount demanded by the deadline cures the notice and the lease stays active; a smaller payment is refused under lease_evt_payment_acceptance.
